collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Only one elder still knows how to make the old masks: teach the young, or let them make their own new masks.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is the last person who knows how to carve the old festival masks, and (subject.his/her) hands are getting stiff. (friend) wants to learn, but also wants to carve masks about (friend.his/her) own life, which (subject) says are not proper masks. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) learns the old way, every cut and curve. It takes two years. (subject) is fierce and patient. At the festival, (friend)'s first old mask is worn, and nobody can tell it was not carved by (subject).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) learns the old masks and carves new ones too: a mask of (friend.his/her) grandmother, a mask of a storm, a mask of the little sister who cries a lot. (subject) is doubtful. At the festival, the new masks are worn beside the old. Nobody minds.
